summary: Server approval subjects now look up every id of an argument that holds a list (memberIds: ['u1', 'u2']): each id is named, refused when it does not exist, or not checkable on its own. Before, a list always fell back to the browser history and warned about unknown ids.
howTo: Nothing to change for single ids. A write tool whose inputEntities name a list argument of a type with an entityLookup now gets server subjects for it: a list of a target or parent reference by default, a reference when approvalSubject.refs names it (refs: ['memberIds']). A missing id refuses the call (approval_subject_not_found); each id counts as one of maxSubjectsPerCall (default 4, at most 16), the rest are not checkable (limit), which onUnavailable: 'block' refuses: raise the limit for tools with longer lists. Subjects of a list share the argument's path, so the card shows one line per argument. A part holds up to 100 subjects (was 20); an older browser shows the history fallback for a larger one. tools refresh reports a composite key with a list argument (approval-subject-invalid); it is not looked up. See docs/approval-subjects.md, Lists of ids.
